hints.title: Which node comes next?
hints.body: At any point, the next node in the merged list is the smaller of the two current heads. What do you need to do after choosing it?

hints.title: Build with a tail
hints.body: Keep a pointer to the last node in the merged list. Compare the two current heads, attach the smaller one to the tail, and advance that list. A dummy head avoids special cases for the first node.

hints.title: Dummy head, then append the rest
hints.body: Create a dummy node and let `tail` point to it. While both heads exist, attach the smaller head and advance that list. When one list ends, attach the other list directly to `tail.next`. Return `dummy.next`.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
dummy = new ListNode(0)
tail = dummy
while first is not empty and second is not empty:
    if first.val <= second.val:
        tail.next = first
        first = first.next
    else:
        tail.next = second
        second = second.next
    tail = tail.next
tail.next = first if first is not empty else second
return dummy.next
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution. Translate it into your language and check it against the examples.
